from.place: ## Proof, first sentence: the conductor equality in Varieties Remark 09NW used in the extension-by-zero argument

title: The conductor ideal restricts isomorphically to one reduced component
statement: Let $Y$ be a reduced scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-reduced-scheme] whose underlying space is the union of finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] $Z_1,\ldots,Z_r$, each with its reduced closed subscheme structure [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $Z\subset Y$ be the reduced closed subscheme supported on $Z_2\cup\cdots\cup Z_r$, let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ be its ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $i_1:Z_1\hookrightarrow Y$ be the component immersion with ideal sheaf $\mathcal J_1$. If $\mathcal I_1$ is the image of $\mathcal I|_{Z_1}$ in $\mathcal O_{Z_1}$, then the natural restriction map $\mathcal I|_{Z_1}\to\mathcal I_1$ is an isomorphism; equivalently, the conductor equality $\mathcal I\cap\mathcal J_1=\mathcal I\mathcal J_1$ holds and restriction identifies the conductor with $\mathcal I_1$.

source.place: Varieties Remark 09NW (varieties-remark-conductor), applied to the reduced component cover
